question: How should compiler-emitted instruction metadata expose complete source ranges without persisting snapshot-local IDs?
decision: Keep optional debug_sources and debug_locations and add an optional debug_ranges section containing source-local half-open byte intervals for existing instruction targets. Derive ranges from M1A1 SourceRange values, validate them against embedded source text, and rebase their artifact-local source indexes during module linking.

wire_shape.entry: main <instruction> = s<source>:<start>:<end> or function f<function> <instruction> = s<source>:<start>:<end>
wire_shape.required_pair: every debug range has a matching debug_locations entry

compatibility_boundary.new_compiler_artifacts: emit a full range for each source-backed instruction
compatibility_boundary.module_products: retain ranges while rebasing source indexes
compatibility_boundary.runtime_display: line and column remain the current diagnostic display

quantitative_gate: All compiler-emitted source-backed instructions in the refreshed artifact corpus have one valid debug range paired with their location; old artifacts still parse and metadata-free runtime behavior is unchanged; repeated C++ emission, Rust dump, module linking, and runtime diagnostics are deterministic.
old_path_deletion_condition: Retain point locations and metadata-free fallback until every supported debug consumer uses the shared range metadata or documents a point-only requirement; never serialize snapshot-local IDs.
